repo.description:
## Impact

The Webflow Trigger node accepted any HTTP POST to its webhook URL without verifying the `x-webflow-signature` HMAC that Webflow attaches to webhook deliveries. An unauthenticated attacker who knows the webhook URL could send a forged request that impersonates a legitimate Webflow event and triggers the workflow with fully attacker-controlled input. Any downstream nodes that act on the event data - creating or updating records, sending messages, or calling internal APIs - would then operate on that forged payload. The patch adds HMAC signature verification to the webhook handler and rejects requests that do not carry a valid signature.

This fix was applied only to Webflow Trigger node version 2.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 1.123.80, 2.39.6 and 2.40.1. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Deactivate any workflows using the Webflow Trigger node if they are not currently required.
- Restrict network-level access to the n8n webhook endpoint to Webflow's published IP ranges only.
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: Missing Webhook Signature Verification in Webflow Trigger Node Allows Forged Event Injection
